passages.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought: “Judah mourns and her gates languish. Her people wail for the land, and a cry goes up from Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message about the drought.
Judah is mourning.
Judah’s gates are weak and suffering.
The people of Judah are sad for their land.
A loud cry rises from Jerusalem.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ עַל־ דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבַּצָּרֽוֹת׃ אָבְלָ֣ה יְהוּדָ֔ה וּשְׁעָרֶ֥יהָ אֻמְלְל֖וּ קָדְר֣וּ לָאָ֑רֶץ וְצִוְחַ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם עָלָֽתָה׃

passages.text: The nobles send their servants for water; they go to the cisterns, but find no water; their jars return empty. They are ashamed and humiliated; they cover their heads.
passages.sermon:
The nobles live in Judah.
A drought covers the land.
The nobles send their servants to get water.
The servants go to the cisterns.
They do not find any water.
The servants return with empty jars.
The nobles feel ashamed.
They feel humiliated.
They cover their heads.
passages.original: וְאַדִּ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם שָׁלְח֥וּ צְעוֹרֵיהֶם לַמָּ֑יִם בָּ֣אוּ עַל־ גֵּבִ֞ים לֹא־ מָ֣צְאוּ מַ֗יִם שָׁ֤בוּ כְלֵיהֶם֙ רֵיקָ֔ם בֹּ֥שׁוּ וְהָכְלְמ֖וּ וְחָפ֥וּ רֹאשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: The ground is cracked because no rain has fallen on the land. The farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeremiah about a drought in Judah.
The ground is cracked.
No rain has fallen on the land.
The farmers feel ashamed.
They cover their heads.
passages.original: בַּעֲב֤וּר הָאֲדָמָה֙ חַ֔תָּה כִּ֛י לֹא־ הָיָ֥ה גֶ֖שֶׁם בָּאָ֑רֶץ בֹּ֥שׁוּ אִכָּרִ֖ים חָפ֥וּ רֹאשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Even the doe in the field deserts her newborn fawn because there is no grass.
passages.sermon:
A doe lives in the field.
She gives birth to a fawn.
She leaves her newborn fawn.
There is no grass in the field.
passages.original: כִּ֤י גַם־ אַיֶּ֙לֶת֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יָלְדָ֖ה וְעָז֑וֹב כִּ֥י לֹֽא־ הָיָ֖ה דֶּֽשֶׁא׃

passages.text: Wild donkeys stand on barren heights; they pant for air like jackals; their eyes fail for lack of pasture.”
passages.sermon:
Wild donkeys stand on the barren hills.
They breathe heavily like jackals.
Their eyes grow weak.
There is no grass for them to eat.
passages.original: וּפְרָאִים֙ עָמְד֣וּ עַל־ שְׁפָיִ֔ם שָׁאֲפ֥וּ ר֖וּחַ כַּתַּנִּ֑ים כָּל֥וּ עֵינֵיהֶ֖ם כִּי־ אֵ֥ין עֵֽשֶׂב׃

passages.text: Although our iniquities testify against us, O LORD, act for the sake of Your name. Indeed, our rebellions are many; we have sinned against You.
passages.sermon:
We have sinned against you, LORD.
Our iniquities testify against us.
We have committed many rebellions.
Act for the sake of your name, LORD.
passages.original: אִם־ עֲוֺנֵ֙ינוּ֙ עָ֣נוּ בָ֔נוּ יְהוָ֕ה עֲשֵׂ֖ה לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־ רַבּ֥וּ מְשׁוּבֹתֵ֖ינוּ לְךָ֥ חָטָֽאנוּ׃

passages.text: O Hope of Israel, its Savior in times of distress, why are You like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stays but a night?
passages.sermon:
God is the Hope of Israel.
God is Israel’s Savior in times of trouble.
Why do You seem like a stranger in this land?
Why do You seem like a traveler who only stays for one night?
passages.original: מִקְוֵה֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מֽוֹשִׁיע֖וֹ בְּעֵ֣ת צָרָ֑ה לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיֶה֙ כְּגֵ֣ר בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּכְאֹרֵ֖חַ נָטָ֥ה לָלֽוּן׃

passages.text: Why are You like a man taken by surprise, like a warrior powerless to save? Yet You are among us, O LORD, and we are called by Your name. Do not forsake us!
passages.sermon:
The people speak to the LORD.
They see the LORD as present among them.
They call the LORD by His name.
They ask the LORD a question.
They say, “Why do You seem like a man who is surprised?”
They say, “Why do You seem like a warrior who cannot save?”
They remind the LORD that He is with them.
They remind the LORD that they are called by His name.
They ask the LORD, “Do not leave us.”
passages.original: לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיֶה֙ כְּאִ֣ישׁ נִדְהָ֔ם כְּגִבּ֖וֹר לֹא־ יוּכַ֣ל לְהוֹשִׁ֑יעַ וְאַתָּ֧ה בְקִרְבֵּ֣נוּ יְהוָ֗ה וְשִׁמְךָ֛ עָלֵ֥ינוּ נִקְרָ֖א אַל־ תַּנִּחֵֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says about this people: “Truly they love to wander; they have not restrained their feet. So the LORD does not accept them; He will now remember their guilt and call their sins to account.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the people of Israel.
The people of Israel love to wander.
They do not restrain their feet.
The LORD does not accept these people.
The LORD will now remember their guilt.
The LORD will call their sins to account.
passages.original: כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה כֵּ֤ן אָֽהֲבוּ֙ לָנ֔וּעַ רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א חָשָׂ֑כוּ וַיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א רָצָ֔ם עַתָּה֙ יִזְכֹּ֣ר עֲוֺנָ֔ם וְיִפְקֹ֖ד חַטֹּאתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to me, “Do not pray for the well-being of this people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a command.
He said, “Do not pray for this people.
Do not ask for their good.
Do not seek their well-being.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י אַל־ תִּתְפַּלֵּ֛ל בְּעַד־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה לְטוֹבָֽה׃

passages.text: Although they may fast, I will not listen to their cry; although they may offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will finish them off by sword and famine and plague.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the people of Judah.
The people may fast.
I will not listen to their cry.
They may offer burnt offerings.
They may bring grain offerings.
I will not accept them.
I will destroy them.
I will use the sword.
I will use famine.
I will use plague.
passages.original: כִּ֣י יָצֻ֗מוּ אֵינֶ֤נִּי שֹׁמֵ֙עַ֙ אֶל־ רִנָּתָ֔ם וְכִ֧י יַעֲל֛וּ עֹלָ֥ה וּמִנְחָ֖ה אֵינֶ֣נִּי רֹצָ֑ם כִּ֗י בַּחֶ֙רֶב֙ וּבָרָעָ֣ב וּבַדֶּ֔בֶר אָנֹכִ֖י מְכַלֶּ֥ה אוֹתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: “Ah, Lord GOD!” I replied, “Look, the prophets are telling them, ‘You will not see the sword or suffer famine, but I will give you lasting peace in this place.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah spoke to the Lord God.
He said, “Ah, Lord God!
The prophets speak to the people.
The prophets say, ‘You will not see the sword.
You will not suffer famine.
God will give you true peace in this place.’”
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה הַנְּבִאִ֜ים אֹמְרִ֤ים לָהֶם֙ לֹֽא־ תִרְא֣וּ חֶ֔רֶב וְרָעָ֖ב לֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ שְׁל֤וֹם אֱמֶת֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָכֶ֔ם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: “The prophets are prophesying lies in My name,” replied the LORD. “I did not send them or appoint them or speak to them. They are prophesying to you a false vision, a worthless divination, the futility and delusion of their own minds.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD said, “The prophets are telling lies.
They claim to speak in My name.
I did not send these prophets.
I did not command them.
I did not speak to them.
They give you false visions.
They practice worthless divination.
They speak the deceit of their own minds.
They prophesy to you from their own hearts, not from Me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י שֶׁ֚קֶר הַנְּבִאִים֙ נִבְּאִ֣ים בִּשְׁמִ֔י לֹ֤א שְׁלַחְתִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א צִוִּיתִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א דִבַּ֖רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם חֲז֨וֹן שֶׁ֜קֶר וְקֶ֤סֶם וֶאֱלוּל וְתַרְמוּת לִבָּ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says about the prophets who prophesy in My name: I did not send them, yet they say, ‘No sword or famine will touch this land.’ By sword and famine these very prophets will meet their end!
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about certain prophets.
These prophets claim to speak in the LORD’s name.
The LORD did not send these prophets.
These prophets say, “No sword will come to this land.”
They also say, “No famine will come to this land.”
The LORD says these prophets are wrong.
The LORD says these prophets will die by the sword.
The LORD says these prophets will die by famine.
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַֽל־ הַנְּבִאִ֞ים הַנִּבְּאִ֣ים בִּשְׁמִי֮ וַאֲנִ֣י לֹֽא־ שְׁלַחְתִּים֒ וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים חֶ֣רֶב וְרָעָ֔ב לֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את בַּחֶ֤רֶב וּבָֽרָעָב֙ יִתַּ֔מּוּ הַנְּבִאִ֖ים הָהֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword. There will be no one to bury them or their wives, their sons or their daughters. I will pour out their own evil upon them.
passages.sermon:
The people listened to the false prophets.
These prophets spoke lies in God’s name.
God did not send these prophets.
The people who believed them will suffer.
They will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem.
Famine and the sword will cause their suffering.
No one will bury them.
No one will bury their wives.
No one will bury their sons.
No one will bury their daughters.
God will pour out their own evil upon them.
passages.original: וְהָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ הֵ֣מָּה נִבְּאִ֣ים לָהֶ֡ם יִֽהְי֣וּ מֻשְׁלָכִים֩ בְּחֻצ֨וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם מִפְּנֵ֣י׀ הָרָעָ֣ב וְהַחֶ֗רֶב וְאֵ֤ין מְקַבֵּר֙ לָהֵ֔מָּה הֵ֣מָּה נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם וּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְנֹֽתֵיהֶ֑ם וְשָׁפַכְתִּ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת־ רָעָתָֽם׃

passages.text: You are to speak this word to them: ‘My eyes overflow with tears; day and night they do not cease, for the virgin daughter of my people has been shattered by a crushing blow, a severely grievous wound.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jeremiah.
God commands Jeremiah to deliver a message to the people.
Jeremiah must say these words to them.
"My eyes overflow with tears.
Tears fall day and night.
My eyes do not stop weeping.
The virgin daughter of my people has been shattered.
She has suffered a crushing blow.
Her wound is very severe."
passages.original: וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה תֵּרַ֨דְנָה עֵינַ֥י דִּמְעָ֛ה לַ֥יְלָה וְיוֹמָ֖ם וְאַל־ תִּדְמֶ֑ינָה כִּי֩ שֶׁ֨בֶר גָּד֜וֹל נִשְׁבְּרָ֗ה בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־ עַמִּ֔י מַכָּ֖ה נַחְלָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: If I go out to the country, I see those slain by the sword; if I enter the city, I see those ravaged by famine! For both prophet and priest travel to a land they do not know.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah is the prophet speaking.
He describes what he sees in Judah during God's judgment.
If I go out to the fields, I see people killed by the sword.
If I enter the city, I see people suffering from famine.
Both the prophet and the priest leave the land.
They go to a land they do not know.
passages.original: אִם־ יָצָ֣אתִי הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ חַלְלֵי־ חֶ֔רֶב וְאִם֙ בָּ֣אתִי הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֖ה תַּחֲלוּאֵ֣י רָעָ֑ב כִּֽי־ גַם־ נָבִ֧יא גַם־ כֹּהֵ֛ן סָחֲר֥וּ אֶל־ אֶ֖רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃ס

passages.text: Have You rejected Judah completely? Do You despise Zion? Why have You stricken us so that we are beyond healing? We hoped for peace, but no good has come, and for the time of healing, but there was only terror.
passages.sermon:
God, You are the Lord of Judah and Zion.
Have You completely rejected Judah?
Do You despise Zion?
Why have You struck us?
We cannot be healed.
We hoped for peace.
No good has come.
We waited for a time of healing.
We found only terror.
passages.original: הֲמָאֹ֨ס מָאַ֜סְתָּ אֶת־ יְהוּדָ֗ה אִם־ בְּצִיּוֹן֙ גָּעֲלָ֣ה נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ מַדּ֙וּעַ֙ הִכִּיתָ֔נוּ וְאֵ֥ין לָ֖נוּ מַרְפֵּ֑א קַוֵּ֤ה לְשָׁלוֹם֙ וְאֵ֣ין ט֔וֹב וּלְעֵ֥ת מַרְפֵּ֖א וְהִנֵּ֥ה בְעָתָֽה׃

passages.text: We acknowledge our wickedness, O LORD, the guilt of our fathers; indeed, we have sinned against You.
passages.sermon:
We speak to the LORD.
We admit our own wickedness.
We also admit the guilt of our fathers.
We have sinned against You, LORD.
passages.original: יָדַ֧עְנוּ יְהוָ֛ה רִשְׁעֵ֖נוּ עֲוֺ֣ן אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֥י חָטָ֖אנוּ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: For the sake of Your name do not despise us; do not disgrace Your glorious throne. Remember Your covenant with us; do not break it.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah speak to God.
They ask God to act for the sake of His name.
They say, “Do not despise us.”
They say, “Do not disgrace Your glorious throne.”
They ask God to remember His covenant with them.
They say, “Do not break Your covenant with us.”
passages.original: אַל־ תִּנְאַץ֙ לְמַ֣עַן שִׁמְךָ֔ אַל־ תְּנַבֵּ֖ל כִּסֵּ֣א כְבוֹדֶ֑ךָ זְכֹ֕ר אַל־ תָּפֵ֥ר בְּרִֽיתְךָ֖ אִתָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Can the worthless idols of the nations bring rain? Do the skies alone send showers? Is this not by You, O LORD our God? So we put our hope in You, for You have done all these things.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
He alone has power over nature.
The idols of the nations are worthless.
These idols cannot bring rain.
The skies themselves do not send showers by their own power.
You, LORD, give rain and showers.
You have done all these things.
We put our hope in You.
passages.original: הֲיֵ֨שׁ בְּהַבְלֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ מַגְשִׁמִ֔ים וְאִם־ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם יִתְּנ֣וּ רְבִבִ֑ים הֲלֹ֨א אַתָּה־ ה֜וּא יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּ֨נְקַוֶּה־ לָּ֔ךְ כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתָ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֵֽלֶּה׃פ
